growth_stages.notes: Optimum temperature for stem/leaf growth is ~30C; growth rate and photosynthesis begin to decline once temperatures reach ~35C.
sources: Bibi et al. 2008/2010, cited in Cotton.org Stress Physiology in Cotton, Ch.1

growth_stages.notes: Reproductive success negatively affected above 28-30C; cotton is highly sensitive during the first five weeks of flowering and boll development. Pollen germination peaks near 28C and declines precipitously above 37C.
growth_stages.reference_detail: Reproductive success negatively affected with temperatures above 28-30C (Oosterhuis & Snider 2011). Fruit retention/boll size decline as mean temperature rises above ~28C, with very low retention above 32C.
sources: Burke et al. 2004 (pollen germination peak 28C, decline >37C)

growth_stages.notes: Very low fruit retention once mean temperatures exceed ~32C; boll abscission 3-5 days after bloom is the dominant heat-stress mechanism.

engine_notes: Cotton has the widest cited range (28-32C) of the four crops because retention decline is gradual rather than a sharp step function. CropHeat uses 30C as the engine default for flowering (mid-point of the cited onset range) and 32C for boll development, both documented here rather than hidden in code.
